instruction: In the open spreadsheet, add a SUM formula in cell B16 that totals all the prices in column B from rows 2 to 14.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(1);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent selected data range A1:E14 in Calc, copied it, opened Writer, used Paste Special with 'LibreOffice 7.3 Spreadsheet' (OLE embed instead of table), attempted to save as price.docx. Failed because data was pasted as embedded object not a Writer table.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select cell ranges in LibreOffice Calc using Name Box, copy with Ctrl+C, open Writer from Calc, navigate Paste Special dialog, use Save As dialog with filename and location selection
metadata.failure_analysis: Model pasted data as OLE spreadsheet object instead of a Writer table. Also missed row 15 (Estimate No.). The compare_docx_tables evaluator failed because content was not in proper docx table format.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a single-app Calc task (entering a SUM formula) within model's demonstrated capability of cell navigation and data entry
metadata.explanation: Task requires entering a SUM formula in cell B16 to total column B prices. Evaluator reads cell B16 value after saving and checks it matches the expected sum of 12374.7 within tolerance.

scoring_breakdown.formula_result: 1.0 - Cell B16 contains correct sum value (12374.7)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads cell B16 from the correct sheet with data_only=True to get the computed formula value
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('expected_value') and expected.get('tolerance')

Minor gap: evaluator only checks the numeric result in B16, not whether B16 actually contains a SUM formula (a hardcoded value of 12374.7 would also pass)
